clue.text: Tested guided missile power at first

indicators.note: these words say the missile and power come first, before the next piece

parts.note: a SAM is a surface-to-air missile, which is guided to its target
P is the standard abbreviation for power in physics
led means guided or steered

explanation.surface: A report that a guided missile was tested, with its power supply checked first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guided' seems to describe the missile, but it supplies LED; 'at first' places SAM and P ahead of it.
explanation.definitionFit: To sample something is to try or taste a portion of it, so sampled means tried out.

clue.text: Prop having increased intensity in game

indicators.note: in means placed inside the word for game

parts.note: a sport is a game
turning the volume up means increasing intensity

explanation.surface: A rugby prop forward raising the intensity of the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prop' suggests the rugby position, but it is a support.
explanation.definitionFit: A prop is something that holds up a structure, which is a support.

clue.text: Girl welcomes a tense English artist

indicators.note: welcomes means takes in, so the girl holds the next two pieces

parts.note: a miss is a girl or young woman
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A young woman greets a nervous English painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri Matisse was the French painter famed for his colourful Fauvist works.

clue.text: Sponge from a sucker being set up

indicators.note: set up in a down entry means raised, so the letters read upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: a sucker is a fool, someone easily duped

explanation.surface: A dupe is being framed, with someone sponging off them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' suggests framing a dupe; in a down clue it means reading upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A loofa is a bath sponge made from the fibrous dried fruit of a gourd.

clue.text: Crafty, stooping to pinch shilling

indicators.note: pinch means squeeze, so the stooping word grips the coin's letter

parts.note: deigning means condescending or stooping to do something
S is the abbreviation for a shilling, an old British coin

explanation.surface: A sly character lowers themselves to steal a shilling.
explanation.walkthrough: A shilling was a pre-decimal British coin. 'pinch' looks like stealing but signals one piece gripping another.
explanation.definitionFit: A designing person is scheming and cunning, so crafty in the sense of artful.

clue.text: Ashes following maiden for fellows?

indicators.note: the ashes come after the maiden, so they follow it in the answer

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
embers are the glowing ashes of a fire

explanation.surface: Looks like a cricket report: the Ashes series following a maiden over, with fellows as players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ashes' suggests the cricket series between England and Australia but means fire remains. The question mark flags fellows of a society as an example of members.
explanation.definitionFit: Fellows of a college or learned society are its members, so the plural nouns match.

clue.text: Thick fog seen around break of day

indicators.note: seen around means placed surrounding, so the mist encloses the letter

parts.note: mist is a light fog

indicators.note: break of day is dawn, its start, so the first letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A dense fog has been observed at dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thick' seems to describe fog, but it is the definition, as in 'the thick of battle'.
explanation.definitionFit: The thick of something is its middle, its busiest point, which is what the midst means.

clue.text: Nice men?

parts.note: reads as pleasant chaps, but Nice is the French city, so this is the French word for gentlemen

explanation.surface: A wistful query about pleasant gentlemen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' at the start hides its capital: it is the city on the French Riviera.
explanation.definitionFit: The French plural title for gentlemen, as used by men in Nice.

clue.text: Great kipper knocking out a cold gourmet

indicators.note: knocking out means removing, so one letter goes from the joined words

parts.note: epic means great or grand
to kipper a fish is to cure it by salting and smoking
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A fine smoked herring cures a gourmet of his cold.
explanation.walkthrough: A kipper is a British smoked herring; here the verb means to cure. 'knocking out' removes one C from EPICCURE.
explanation.definitionFit: An epicure is someone with refined taste in food and drink, a connoisseur or gourmet.

clue.text: Browse with boosted connection finding stuff

parts.note: to surf the internet is to browse

indicators.note: boosted means raised, so in a down entry the word for connection reads upwards

parts.note: a tie is a connection or link

explanation.surface: Browsing the web on a faster connection, finding material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boosted connection' suggests faster broadband but turns TIE into EIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To surfeit is to overfeed or glut someone, the verb sense of stuff.

clue.text: Wretched end over European Union's accepting nothing

indicators.note: over signals turning the word for end upside down, so it reads backwards

parts.note: a tip is the end of something, like a pencil tip

indicators.note: accepting means taking something in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: EU is the European Union, with the S of the possessive
O is the figure zero, meaning nothing

explanation.surface: A bleak political commentary: the European Union reaching a wretched end, getting nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end' tempts a last-letter pick, but it is a synonym here; 'over' turns that synonym round, and 'accepting' takes the zero into the possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Piteous means deserving pity, so it describes something wretched or pitiful.

clue.text: One lying about securing international portfolio

indicators.note: securing means holding something fast, so the idler wraps around the other letter

parts.note: a dosser is an idler or a homeless person who sleeps rough, someone lying about

explanation.surface: An idler gets hold of an international portfolio of investments.
explanation.walkthrough: DOSSER is British slang for a layabout or someone sleeping rough.
explanation.definitionFit: A dossier is a file of papers on a subject, and a portfolio is such a collection of documents.

clue.text: Morons laugh tactlessly seizing offensive

indicators.note: seizing means grabbing hold of, so the letters are caught within the phrase

explanation.surface: Idiots laughing tactlessly while a military offensive is being seized.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs through 'MorONS LAUGH Tactlessly'.
explanation.definitionFit: An offensive is a fierce attack, the same as an assault or onslaught's sense of a violent charge.

clue.text: Initially is not upset regarding excessive temper

indicators.note: initially tells us to take the opening letter of each of the next five words

explanation.surface: Advice that, at first, one should not be upset about someone's excessive temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'temper' looks like a noun meaning anger, but it is a verb: to toughen or harden.
explanation.definitionFit: To temper steel is to harden it, and to inure someone is to harden them to hardship.

clue.text: Force shot occasionally hooked on driving area

indicators.note: on means placed after, so these letters follow the driving area

parts.note: a tee is the area on a golf course from which you drive off

indicators.note: a hooked golf shot curves the wrong way, so the picked letters turn back on themselves
occasionally means every so often, so only alternate letters of the word are kept

explanation.surface: A golfing scene: a shot that is hooked off the tee, as happens from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' takes H and T from 'shot'; 'hooked' turns them to TH.
explanation.definitionFit: A law with teeth has real power to compel; teeth means force or effectiveness.

clue.text: Drop of the hard stuff?

parts.note: a drop of the hard stuff sounds like a tot of spirits, but here it is a frozen drop of rain falling from the sky

explanation.surface: An offer of a small measure of strong liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the hard stuff' is slang for spirits; here it is literally solid ice.
explanation.definitionFit: A pellet of ice falling in a storm is a frozen, hard droplet of precipitation.

clue.text: It's unwise being disrespectful about Republican

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the cheeky word goes around the other letter

parts.note: impudent means cheeky or disrespectful

explanation.surface: A warning that being rude about a Republican politician is an unwise move.
explanation.definitionFit: Imprudent means lacking prudence or good sense, which is what unwise describes.

clue.text: Part super for Mermaids actress?

indicators.note: part means a portion, so the letters are a section of the following words

explanation.surface: An actress with a super role in the film Mermaids.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs through 'suPER FOR MERmaids'. The question mark flags an actress as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: An actress is one example of someone who entertains on stage or screen.

clue.text: Warning of endless damage facing Netflix addict?

definitions.note: the definition is a noun: a sign or warning of what is to come

indicators.note: endless means the final letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: harm means damage
a binger is someone who binge-watches, typically on a streaming service like Netflix

explanation.surface: Someone hooked on Netflix being warned of the endless harm it does.
explanation.definitionFit: A harbinger is an omen or forerunner that announces something approaching, so it serves as a warning.

clue.text: Nelson and Hardy's first speech unfinished

indicators.note: first means the opening letter of the word before it
unfinished means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: an oration is a formal speech

explanation.surface: Nelson and Hardy at Trafalgar, with a speech left incomplete.
explanation.walkthrough: Hardy was Nelson's flag captain at Trafalgar, famed for 'Kiss me, Hardy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Admiral Lord Nelson's first name was Horatio.

clue.text: Half grand, Queen uplifted governments

indicators.note: uplifted means raised, so in a down entry the pieces read upwards

parts.note: semi is a prefix meaning half
G is slang for a grand, a thousand
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: The Queen raises half a thousand pounds while governments come and go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uplifted' turns SEMIGER into the answer reading up the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A regime is a government, especially an authoritarian one, so the plurals match.

clue.text: Aggregate's put round opening of petrol reservoirs

indicators.note: put round means placed surrounding, so the totals enclose the letter

parts.note: aggregates are totals or sums, the 's read as a plural

indicators.note: opening of points to the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Looks like a statistic about petrol reserves: totals put around the start of supply.
explanation.definitionFit: A sump is a pit or well collecting liquid, such as an engine's oil reservoir.

clue.text: The first person seized by robber getting closer

indicators.note: seized by means held within, so the robber surrounds the pronoun

parts.note: a mugger is a robber who attacks people in the street
I is the first person pronoun

explanation.surface: I am grabbed by a thief who is getting nearer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'closer' looks like nearer but means more humid, as close weather is.
explanation.definitionFit: Close weather is muggy, stuffy and humid, so closer means muggier.

clue.text: Certain about you French Germany stitched up

indicators.note: about means around, so the certain word surrounds the French word

parts.note: sure means certain
tu is French for you
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: A claim that the French and Germans definitely framed you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stitched up' suggests framed but is literal sewing of a wound.
explanation.definitionFit: Sutured means sewn closed, as a surgeon closes a wound with stitches.

clue.text: Sees red and scraps conserving energy

indicators.note: conserving means keeping something within, so the cloth scraps hold the letter

parts.note: rags are scraps of cloth
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone gets furious about scraps of food or material while trying to save energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scraps' could be fights, but here it means bits of cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: To see red is to become furious, which is what someone who rages does.

clue.text: Scorn embroiling premier back in public eye

indicators.note: embroiling means involving or taking in, so the snub surrounds the turned word

parts.note: a slight is a snub, an act of scorn

indicators.note: back means the word for premier reads backwards

parts.note: premier means top or first

explanation.surface: Scornful treatment draws a prime minister back into public attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns TOP into POT.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the spotlight means being the focus of public attention, as a stage light picks out a performer.

clue.text: Fish travel on ice

definitions.meaning: a flat fish of the ray family, eaten as food
to glide over ice on blades

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a flat ray-like fish and the act of gliding over ice on bladed boots.

clue.text: Inclined to have hard time

parts.note: lean times are hard times, with little money or food

explanation.surface: Someone disposed to endure a difficult period.
explanation.definitionFit: Inclined means tilted or sloping, which is what something that leant did.

clue.text: Vault over line, a fair game

parts.note: a vault is an underground burial chamber, a tomb
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: An athlete leaps over a line in a sporting event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vault' suggests a leap but is a burial chamber. TOMBOLA is a raffle game at British fairs and fêtes, where prizes are won from a drum of tickets.
explanation.definitionFit: A tombola is a lottery game typically run at a fair or fête, so it is literally a fair game.

clue.text: More beefy mass, one consumed by consumer

parts.note: M is the physics symbol for mass

indicators.note: consumed by means swallowed inside, so the eater wraps around the numeral

parts.note: an eater is one who consumes food
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A food review: a heftier lump of meat, eaten up by a hungry diner.
explanation.definitionFit: Beefy and meaty both describe something substantial or brawny, so more beefy is a comparative synonym.

clue.text: Old boy reportedly perceived to be off-colour

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

indicators.note: reportedly means as said aloud, so the word for perceived is replaced by one sounding the same

parts.note: seen means perceived

explanation.surface: A former schoolboy is said to have been noticed looking ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off-colour' suggests unwell but here means risqué or indecent.
explanation.definitionFit: Off-colour jokes are rude or smutty, so the sense is indecent.

clue.text: Socialist, without ceremony, rejected left

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the socialist sits around the turned word

parts.note: a red is a socialist or communist

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the word for ceremony reads backwards

parts.note: a rite is a ceremony

explanation.surface: A socialist, leaving without a send-off, rejected the left wing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' looks like the political wing but means departed. 'rejected' turns RITE into ETIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has retired has withdrawn or departed, so has left.
